about: Every ISSPG icpg variable sorted into input / optimisation / fixed / dependent. 'cad_variables' are the 117 variables ISSPG icpg writes to CADs/ISSPG/isspg_icpg_equations_onshape.txt, in that order (this gearbox has no other equation file); 'code_only' are values the code uses but does not write to the CAD file, plus every config key the CAD does not use; 'unused_config_blocks' are config blocks ISSPG never reads. tests/test_variable_categories.py checks the lists against the code and re-evaluates every formula and lookup; docs/variables/icpg.md is generated from this file (python tools/variables/render.py).

categories.input: chosen parts and material: the motor's dimensions and torque, the motor driver's mount dimensions, the gear material's allowable stress
categories.optimisation: searched by the optimiser: teeth, module, number of planets
categories.fixed: constants that don't depend on the design: clearances, wall thicknesses, fastener and bearing choices, feature sizes, the gear standard
categories.dependent: computed from the variables above, by a formula, a catalogue lookup (bearings, bolts, nuts) or a rule the code applies (the tooth-stress rule for face widths)

confidence.high: the code reads it directly from one source, or computes it with an explicit formula
confidence.medium: the code is clear, but the category is a judgement call (see the reason)
confidence.low: can't be decided from the code alone

cad_variables.name: fw_s_calc
cad_variables.rule: two stress widths, b = FOS x Ft x qe x qk / (gear_allowable_stress x module): b1 for the sun - big planet mesh (module, Ft from serviceFactor x motor_peak_torque at the sun, qe from the sun-planet contact ratio, qk from Ns) and b2 for the small planet - ring mesh (module_s, qk from Np_s); then, if b1 + b2 < 2 x planet_bearing_width + planet_bearing_gap, each planet gear is raised to at least planet_bearing_width + planet_bearing_gap / 2 (one bearing per gear, half the gap each; mitStressAnalysisMinFacewidth); fw_s_calc = b1; then the two planet steps (big + small + planet_step_gap_mm) must fit the stator height less gear_axial_margin_mm: when they are longer, all four widths are scaled by (stator_height - gear_axial_margin_mm - planet_step_gap_mm) / (big + small), so the capped gears carry the same fraction of the torque
cad_variables.reason: sun face width from the tooth-stress rule, scaled by the stator-height cap when it applies: fixed by the optimisation variables, the motor torque, the gear material, the safety factors and the cap

cad_variables.name: sun_hub_dia
cad_variables.formula: (Rotor_OD - standard_clearance_1_5mm * 2) if (rotor_mount_hole_PCD + rotor_mount_hole_dia + standard_clearance_1_5mm * sun_hub_clearance_multiple) > Rotor_OD else (rotor_mount_hole_PCD + rotor_mount_hole_dia + standard_clearance_1_5mm * sun_hub_clearance_multiple)
cad_variables.reason: sun hub: sized to the rotor's mount holes plus a margin of sun_hub_clearance_multiple x standard_clearance_1_5mm (config), capped at the rotor's outer diameter less two clearances

cad_variables.name: fw_p_b
cad_variables.rule: two stress widths, b = FOS x Ft x qe x qk / (gear_allowable_stress x module): b1 for the sun - big planet mesh (module, Ft from serviceFactor x motor_peak_torque at the sun, qe from the sun-planet contact ratio, qk from Ns) and b2 for the small planet - ring mesh (module_s, qk from Np_s); then, if b1 + b2 < 2 x planet_bearing_width + planet_bearing_gap, each planet gear is raised to at least planet_bearing_width + planet_bearing_gap / 2 (one bearing per gear, half the gap each; mitStressAnalysisMinFacewidth); fw_p_b = b1 (raised); then the two planet steps (big + small + planet_step_gap_mm) must fit the stator height less gear_axial_margin_mm: when they are longer, all four widths are scaled by (stator_height - gear_axial_margin_mm - planet_step_gap_mm) / (big + small), so the capped gears carry the same fraction of the torque
cad_variables.reason: big-planet face width from the tooth-stress rule, raised to hold its bearing and scaled by the stator-height cap

cad_variables.name: fw_s_used
cad_variables.formula: motor_height if ((stator_ID - bearing_OD) / 2 < standard_clearance_1_5mm * 2 and (standard_clearance_1_5mm * 2 + sun_sec_carrier_bearing_height - (sun_bottom_casing_bearing_height + standard_clearance_1_5mm - sun_coupler_hub_thickness) + sec_carrier_thickness + clearance_planet + fw_p_s + fw_p_b) < motor_height) else (standard_clearance_1_5mm * 2 + sun_sec_carrier_bearing_height - (sun_bottom_casing_bearing_height + standard_clearance_1_5mm - sun_coupler_hub_thickness) + sec_carrier_thickness + clearance_planet + fw_p_s + fw_p_b)
cad_variables.reason: printed sun length: the stack of bearings, hub, carrier and planet widths, but at least the motor height when the stator's radial clearance around the output bearing is below a hard-coded 2 x standard_clearance_1_5mm (a two-case floor rule; the plan asks whether the 2 is geometry or tuning)

code_only.name: pressure_angle_rad
code_only.reason: pressure angle in radians (code attribute pressure_angle)

code_only.name: motor_peak_torque
code_only.reason: motor torque the gears are sized for (peak torque under the default rating setting); sets the face widths

code_only.name: gear_allowable_stress
code_only.reason: allowable tooth stress of the gear material, chosen with the material mode (3dp: PLA, metal: steel); sets the face widths

code_only.name: FOS
code_only.reason: factor of safety in the tooth-stress rule (the ISSPG default is 1.2)

code_only.name: serviceFactor
code_only.reason: service factor on the motor torque in the tooth-stress rule

code_only.name: planet_bearing_gap
code_only.reason: axial gap between the two planet bearings (one in each planet gear); with the bearing width it sets the smallest planet and ring width

code_only.name: sun_hub_clearance_multiple
code_only.reason: margin around the sun hub's bolt circle, in multiples of standard_clearance_1_5mm (4); used for the sun hub and the bottom-casing bearing request; one shared key name across the gearbox types

code_only.name: maxGearboxDiameter
code_only.reason: largest gearbox diameter the optimiser may use (gearbox_runner max_diameter): the stator's inner diameter times a factor (the gears sit inside the frameless outrunner)

code_only.name: module_s
code_only.reason: the small module (small planet, ring): searched by the optimiser loop, but not in the CAD file (which has one module; ISSUES bug 18)

code_only.name: bearingIDClearance_3DP
code_only.reason: constant from the ICPG 3DP design parameters

code_only.name: actuator_width
code_only.formula: fw_s_used + bearing_height + sun_coupler_hub_thickness + standard_clearance_1_5mm * 3.5 + sun_bottom_casing_bearing_height + bearing_retainer_thickness
code_only.reason: axial width: both motor-case walls plus the motor case height, written to the results CSV

code_only.name: fw_limit_mm
code_only.reason: the widest gear the stator height allows: the stator height less gear_axial_margin_mm (the width cap of the stress rule)
